articleTitle: Integrated Radar and Communication Based on DS-UWB
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Tremendous efforts have been devoted to develop the UWB technology for radar and communication applications over the past decades. With the rapidly incremental demand, there is something in exploring of integrated UWB radar and communication system for reducing cost, minimizing the radar cross and probability of intercept, etc. This paper presents an integration system of radar and communication based on direct sequence UWB (DS-UWB). It utilizes different PN code to spread the spectrum of radar and communication data to avoid jamming mutually. The simulation over an ideal AWGN channel shows that the system can work perfectly

articleTitle: Practical Application of Ultra-Wideband Radars
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The possibility of ultra-wideband (UWB) radar use in various fields for remote measuring of the object's motion at short distance is considered. As an illustration UWB radar in medicine for remote measuring of patient's heart activity and respiration is shown. The measuring method is described and practical results of tests are cited. The opportunity of radar application in the other areas is described

articleTitle: Foams Absorbing Material Properties in Range of 38-52 GHz
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The experimental results of measurements of electromagnetic wave reflection for some specimens of water foam for various time of their existence in free space for frequency range 38 - 52 GHz are presented. Thickness of specimens was 80 mm, the range of foaming ratio was from 69 till 173. It was possible to select separately the reflections from the front and rear interface of specimens. It has been shown that reflective characteristics of the foam specimens depend from the specimen foaming ratio and time of foam existence.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Signal Processing Algorithms for Radars and Sodars
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: In this paper we use statistical approach to synthesize algorithms for digital signal processing in UWB noise radar and sodar. Parametrical and non-parametrical algorithms are synthesized and analyzed. Experimental check is done on the basis of developed acoustic physical model which is used to build a noise sodar prototype. Developed algorithms can be used in noise radars for different applications. The use of the UWB noise signal provides a very high resolution both in speed and range

articleTitle: Time Domain Antenna Measurement Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: To carry out measurements in frequency domain (FD) indoors the expensive anechoic chambers are necessary. Time domain (TD) method allows to eliminate the reflections from adjacent objects. Therefore it is possible to carry out TD measurements indoors without anechoic chamber. The TD method lets to use considerably cheap signal generator and receiver than those used in FD. The additional advantage of outdoor TD measurement systems is interference immunity. The report contains indoor and outdoor TD antenna measurement systems utilizing Geozondas Ltd equipment description. The errors are analyzing. It is possible to use the same signal receiver, i.e. sampling oscilloscope, both in frequency and time domain measurements. The TD antenna measurements are possible to carry out in far and near fields

articleTitle: Software for Image Simulation in Ground Penetrating Radar Problems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The computer program LtSEMPGt simulating GPR profiles that can display the subsurface ground structure consisting of any quantity of objects and layers of any geometrical form and with any electrical parameters, has been developed for wide application. The structure and general characteristics of basic modules of the developed software have been considered. The examples of some calculations have been cited

articleTitle: Measuring Instruments of Powerful UWB Emp Parameters
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Measuring instruments used in tests of radio electronic apparatus for stability to influence of ultrashort electromagnetic pulses (UWB-SP) have been considered. It is showed that strip transducers are optimal as primary UWB-SP transducers at repetition rate up to 10 MHz. The transducer on the basis of TEM horn has been created. The transducer permits to carry out the measurements of UWB-SP parameters at repetition rate up to 1 GHz. Compact autonomous digital measurer of maximal values of electric intensity for rapid estimation of UWB-SP intensity levels has been described

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Signals: Theory, Simulation and Digital Processing
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The propagation of the pulse ultrawideband (UWB) signals in plasma media, in particular, in the near-to-Earth's plasma layers was simulated. The dispersive distortions of the UWB signal in that media were estimated. The absorption dispersion and the scattering dispersion were taken into consideration. The radar equation for the distributed target location with UWB signals was modified. The wavelet analysis of the UWB signals was performed. The obtained results with the results of the short-time Fourier transform processing were compared and in new specially constructed format were shown. New set of the analytical wavelets based on the atomic functions and called as the Kravchenko-Rvachev analytical wavelets was proposed. Two new types of UWB signals called as non-linear and fractal UWB signals were suggested. Numerical characteristics for created models of that UWB signal types were calculated. Two time-frequency transforms were proposed to apply for UWB signal analysis

articleTitle: The Irregular-Shaped Fractal Antennas for Ultra Wideband Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design of a multiband fractal antenna of irregular shape using two-dimensional fractal clusters. The algorithm of generating fully reproducible fractal clusters is developed. The multiband behavior of the fractal-cluster based antennas is studied by means of numerical analysis. In comparison to regular-shaped fractal antennas more frequency bands and better matching are achieved. The spatial-frequency antenna characteristics are studied under feeding point displacements. As shown by numerical results, small displacements of feeding point allow to control the radiation pattern in certain frequency bands. The larger feeding point displacements are demonstrated to shift antenna frequency bands

articleTitle: 2D Imaging Algorithm for the Evaluation of UWB B-Scans
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband imaging radar system using B-scans for the target identification. The two dimensional inverse boundary scattering transform was successfully applied for through-wall imaging applications. Using this algorithm it is not only possible to detect the target but also to reconstruct the surface curvature of a cylinder behind a wall. Moreover, it is shown that only 24 different positions of the antennas are sufficient to estimate the target shape which results in a low computation time

articleTitle: Ultra Low Frequency Sounding and Tomography of Earth Crust
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Methods of the ultra low-frequency electromagnetic sounding of the conductivity into the earth crust based on wideband (in the frequency range 0.001-1000 Hz) measurements of electromagnetic fields using both natural and artificial sources of are considered. The inverse problem is solved to retrieve continuous one-dimensional profiles of conductivity using iterative approach for the non-linear integral equation derived from Maxwell's equations. A tomography method that uses many-frequency data of the 2D electromagnetic scanning along the earth surface is also proposed. The retrieval of the 3D structure of the conductivity in this method is based on the solution of the 3D integral equation that can be reduced to the convolution equation with respect to lateral co-ordinates in the frameworks of Born approximation

articleTitle: Radiators of Ultrashort Electomagnetic Pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The description of set of spark and semiconductor UWB EMP radiators has been presented. Investigation results have been presented

articleTitle: Photonic Beamforming in Ultra-Wideband Phased Antenna Arrays: Present State and Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper reflects the state-of-the-art of new and rapidly growing field, dealing with beamforming in ultra-wideband (UWB) phased antenna arrays (PAA) based on photonic technology. Principal attention is focused on active phased antenna arrays radiating/receiving ultra-wideband and ultra-short radio- and video-pulses of ~1 ns time duration, named in the paper RP PAA and VP PAA, correspondingly. For both RP PAA and VP PAA the critical problems of insertion losses and thermal stability are characterized. Estimations made for insertion losses and thermal stability of true time delays in RP PAA and VP PAA fiber-optic beamforming systems confirm the practicability of photonic beamforming in UWB RP PAA and UWB VP PAA

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Transient Processes in Open Resonant Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper discusses scalar and vector initial boundary value model problems for two- and three-dimensional telegraphy and wave equations describing the scattering of transient waves on compact objects in unbounded domains of the spaces. The paper also presents novel results associated with the algorithmization and solution of these boundary value problems describing transformations of pulsed electromagnetic waves

articleTitle: Pulse-Doppler UWB Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The paper contains measurement results of moving targets by pulse-Doppler UWB radar. The description of a radar, principle of operation and technical specification are presented. Conditions and results of measurements are described. Feature of the presented measurements: Doppler signals of linear moving targets whose linear sizes exceed resolution of radar

articleTitle: Neural Network Application for Dielectric Structure Parameter Determination by Multifrequency Methods
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Application of neural network ideology for layered dielectric structure nondestructive testing is under consideration. The 3-layered feed-forward with activation function as a sigmoid (S-shaped) was chosen. Time-domain signals synthesized from ultrawideband data is used as input signal. Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm was used for training of the network. Some results of numerical simulation for two-layered structure with air insertion in presence of Gaussian additive noise are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Combining Polarimetry with SEM in Radar Backscattering for Target Identification
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: In identifying radar targets based on the poles (resonances) in the singularity expansion method (SEM), there is additional information to be gained from the residues. The polarizations of the substructure resonances can also be used as a target signature. In addition, the relative times of arrival of the various resonances at the radar can also be used as another way to construct a target image

articleTitle: Propagation of Spherical Transient Electromagnetic Wave Through Radially Inhomogeneous Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The nonstationary three-dimensional electrodynamic problem is transformed into the problem for one-dimensional evolutionary equations by means of the construction of modal basis for electromagnetic field with arbitrary time dependence. Transient electromagnetic fields in infinite space filled with inhomogeneous in radial direction transient medium without losses are presented by spherical modes. The completeness of the basis is proved by means of Weyl's Theorem about orthogonal splitting of Hilbert space. The expansion coefficients of transient electromagnetic field are found from the set of evolutionary equations which describe independent propagation of the modes. The transient electromagnetic field can be found directly without Fourier transform.

articleTitle: Antenna-Circuit-Signal Co-Design for UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: We analyze UWB signal transmission based on combining full-wave EM solutions and equivalent circuits that account for signal dispersion caused by terminal-loaded dipole antennas operating across UWB channels. First, full-wave EM modeling supplies channel numerical transmission functions while their network interpretations provide some useful system-level insight on the collective impact of used antenna geometrical shapes, transmitter-receiver front-end impedances and transmitter driving waveforms. For this, several important performance merits can be considered in frequency domain (FD) and time domain (TD) including energy transmission efficiency, confinement time of pulsed energy, group delay deviation and others. All numerical results are given in a normalized form that makes them scalable to any particular geometry-frequency-time range of interest

articleTitle: A Ground Penetrating UWB Radar System
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A new low-cost pulse based ultra-wideband radar system working up to 6.4 GHz has been developed. The main focus was on the use of cheap off the shelf components. Pulse generation in the transmitter was solved with a simple transistor circuitry. In the receiver the down conversion is realized with a sampling phase detector combined with a direct digital synthesizer. To control the radar system and for transmitting the digitized data to the PC a USB-controller is used

articleTitle: Bandwidth Properties of a Loop Antenna of Cold Plasma of a Gas Discharge
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The results of research of internal and external characteristics of a microwave loop antenna produced on a basis of cold plasma of a gas discharge are presented. It is shown that frequency properties of the plasma antenna by input impedance and by radiation characteristics exceed the relevant parameters of usual dipole loop aerials

articleTitle: Development of Standard Complex for Measuring Instruments of Pulse Electric and Magnetic Intensities
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The history of development of Russian state special standard of units of pulse electric and magnetic intensities is briefly described. The characteristics of acting standard reproducing UWB-SP with front up to 0.3 ns have been presented. The results of preliminary experiments showing the possibility of standard UWB-SP generation with front no more than 30 ps have been described

articleTitle: The Research and Application of UWB Based Industrial Network
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: With the success of wireless technologies, standard wireless technologies are envisioned for the deployment in industrial environments as well. Comparing with the conventional wireless communication technology, the ultra-wideband (UWB) radio has its unique characteristics, wider band, higher speed rate, lower power spectrum density (PSD) and stronger anti-jamming etc. The problems that should be solved and frameworks for UWB based industrial network are analyzed. The design and strategy of MAC and routing protocols are proposed. A position based routing strategy is presented. It may provide the implementation base for future MAC and protocols in the industrial network

articleTitle: Antenna Device for Analysis of Space-Time Vector Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The wideband antenna device for electromagnetic field polarization characteristics research is presented in the report. The key features of the device are in its structure based on the use of wideband radiator (receiving antenna) that allows radiating (receiving) two waves with circular polarization of opposite directions at the same time and also a signal-processing channel. A plane two-thread spiral antenna with two excitation points is proposed as a wideband radiator. The type of radiator was chosen because of its ability to keep directional characteristics high in the wide frequency range, retain the invariable position of local phase center and constant input impedance. The signal-processing channel includes two frequency converters and narrowband summarizing-and-differentiating device. The following things are also presented in the paper: generalized form of electromagnetic field representation as the space-time vector signals; mathematical equations for the needed electromagnetic field polarization components isolation and their synthesis; the estimation of the errors that appear while calculating the structure of the electromagnetic field. There also a way of wideband omni-polarization antenna device calibration was recommended in the paper

articleTitle: Propagation of High-Frequency Current Waves Along Periodical Thin-Wire Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The homogeneous problem of propagation of current along a thin wire of arbitrary geometric form near the ground by the using of the full-wave transmission line theory has been reduced to a Shrodinger-like differential equation with a "potential" depending on the geometry of the wire and on frequency. This "potential" is a complex-valued quantity that corresponds to radiation losses in the initial electrodynamics problems or corresponds to absorption of the particles in the quantum mechanic analogy. If the wire structure is quasi periodical (i.e., it consists from a finite number of identical sections), the "potential" can be approximately represented as a set of periodically arranged identical potentials. We use a formalism of transfer matrix and find an analytical expression for the transmission coefficient of the finite number of periodically located non-uniformities which also contains the scattering data for one non-uniformity. The obtained result gives the possibility to investigate forbidden and allowed frequency zones which are typical for periodic structure

articleTitle: UWB Radars for Chalenging Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A number of challenging radar applications (such as antipersonnel mine detection and human being detection) has been discussed. In these applications UWB technology has a number of advantages of over the traditional narrow-band approach, in particular very high positioning accuracy, rigidity to multi-path propagation and target classification abilities. On a number of examples recent advances of UWB technology in radar have been demonstrated and remaining challenges have been discussed

articleTitle: Test and Standard Sources of Electromagnetic Pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The results and perspectives of developments and investigations of electromagnetic pulse sources for test and metrological purposes at pulse duration up to tens of picoseconds have been presented

articleTitle: LCR with a Traveling Wave Pulse Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The work is devoted to investigations aiming at developing Harmuth's large current radiator, which radiates effectively electromagnetic field ultra wideband (UWB) pulses. The radiator driven by the traveling wave pulse generator that replaces a return loop has been examined. The spatial dependence of parameters of radiated filed pulses of LCR with a reflector has been investigated

articleTitle: UWB Signal Generation, Acquisition and Processing using Wavelet Functions
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Over the past 15 years, extensive research work has been carried out to develop the ultra-wideband (UWB) technology for communication applications, and to resolve the practical challenges in implementing an efficient UWB communication system. In this paper, we present an overview of the application of wavelet functions for UWB communication system. The focus will be on the UWB signal processing. Following a brief review of the characteristics of application specific UWB signal, application of wavelet functions in UWB signal generation, acquisition, and processing will be described

articleTitle: UWB Signals, SA Perspectives in Radar Guidance
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Now, active or semiactive guidance of antiair missile is commonly implemented using narrowband radar illumination signals. But the usage of wideband signals and inverse aperture synthesis for that purpose can give the new capabilities to the target tracking and missile guidance algorithms. Some simulation results are given in confirmation of that statement

articleTitle: Two Modes of Excitation of the UWB/SP Transmitting Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The comparison of two modes of excitation of the transmitting ultra wideband (UWB) short pulse (SP) antenna has been made in the given work. There have been considered situations when the energy is stored either in a concentrated capacitance or directly in the antenna itself. The results of experimental investigations demonstrating the advantage of energy storage directly in the antenna have been presented too. This mode of excitation permits to decrease considerably the energy consumed from the power supply during pulse generation

articleTitle: A Bell-Shaped Planar Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Results of numerical investigation of the influence of an ultra wideband dipole profile on the input impedance and radiation pattern of bow-tie antennas are presented. A new bell-shaped planar dipole antenna is proposed for UWB communications in the frequency range 3.1-10.6 GHz. A printed design of the antenna has return loss less than -10 dB and gain>2 over the whole frequency range

articleTitle: Development of Surveillance and Tracking Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A high-resolution surveillance and tracking radar has been recently developed and tested at the Institute of Radio Astronomy. The radar is a monopulse, all-weather radar with mechanical beam steering. It works in a pulse mode, and a coherent FFT-based signal processing is utilized. The radar is equipped with a clutter suppression system and with a Kalman filtering scheme for trajectory calculation and extrapolation. The radar is suitable for long-range surveillance with a small volume-scanning time and for tracking of highly dynamic, low-sized targets. This paper describes the setup of this radar, its main components, and the signal processing technique used

articleTitle: Estimation of the Accuracy of the Antenna Near Field Amplitude and Phase Determination in the Frequency Band by Measurements of Impulse Signals Parameters
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The purpose of work is to estimate statistical characteristics of the amplitude and phase distribution of the antenna near field by impulse signals measurements. Research methods are based on the statistical theory of antennas and allow to estimate the accuracy of the restored radiation pattern (RP) in the frequency band using the known statistics of the near field measurements

Author Keywords: accuracy of restoration of radiation pattern

articleTitle: Near-Field Distribution of Linear and Aperture Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: On the basis of Hertz potential technique the expressions for component of the electromagnetic radiation field of aperture and wire antennas have been derived for arbitrarily distance from the antenna to the point of observation. The analysis of amplitude and phase characteristics of orthogonal components of electromagnetic field as a function of observation point coordinate has been carried out.

articleTitle: Excitation of Linear Antenna by a Non-Symmetric Exponential Pulse
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: We calculate explicitly the radiation pattern for linear antenna with uniform distribution excited by a current pulse with exponential fronts. For a specific experimental form of non-symmetric exciting current pulse we demonstrate that our approximation is better for both the incident current pulse and the resulting energetic directivity than the approximation with the Gauss-like pulse. We study the dependence of the directivity from the signal shape and the length of antenna. In particular, we consider symmetric and step-like pulses

articleTitle: Charge Transport by a Pulse E-Wave in a Waveguide Filled with Conductive Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: An E-wave in a waveguide filled with a conductive medium excites longitudinal conductivity currents. Total flow of this current through a cross-section is nonzero that means that charge is transported by a pulse E-wave. This phenomenon is studied in the paper using analytical technique based on modal expansion of the fields in the time domain. Volume conductivity charges created by a pulse wave are found. The problem of diffraction of a pulse E-wave by an interface of a conductive medium is considered as well. Behavior of transient fields and surface charges at the interface was also examined. It was shown that a pulse wave excites surface wave at the interface that results in transversal resonance with relaxation time much greater than that of the conductive medium

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Signals and Wigner Transform
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The Wigner transform well known as the square time-frequency transform from Cohen class for the ultrawideband signal analysis was proposed. The general properties, advantages and disadvantages of the Wigner transform were discussed. Some analytical results of the Wigner transform spectral density calculations for the model ultrawideband signals were shown. That models and the ultrawideband signal models based on the atomic functions were analyzed numerically with the Wigner transform and were discussed. The results of the ultrawideband signal analysis performed the Wigner transform usage with ones based on the short-time Fourier transform were compared

articleTitle: Separation of the Sum of Sinusoid and Impulses
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: New approach for solving problem of a separation of the sum of sinusoidal signal and short or ultrashort impulses is proposed. Setting a considered problem contains assumptions that sinusoidal signal is single and impulses are strictly finite in the time, but parameters of sinusoidal signal and impulses are unknown a priori. Instead of standard least squares criterion, based on minimization of discrepancy square, the criterion of the minimum of the "length of discrepancy" of solution is used. Results of numerical simulations are presented as well

articleTitle: Small-Sized Ship Navigating Radar Boosted Accuracy Rating for the Purposes Short-Range Shipping Season
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: It is shown, that the modern ship radars of a decimeter and centimetric wave band do not obey safety of float in the constrained and foreshore waters because of poor efficiency of definition accurate parameters and, hence, small information. The use of small duration of an outgoing pulse (about 70 nsec) gives high-resolution capability on range, however does not provide by virtue of lines of causes of high-resolution capability on an azimuth. In the report one of the ways of mastering the accuracy of a radar with the help of use of the "radar-attachment" working in a millimeter wave band is considered. Two types of possible build-up of the antenna systems which can be used in the specified radars of boosted precision that will enable to carry out high-resolution capability on a direction presented

articleTitle: Power Parameters of Ultra-Wideband Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper deals with the mathematical model of functional power parameters based on the singular expansion of complex normalized scattering matrix of the antenna array. Problem of broadband matching of the antenna array is discussed. Results of computer simulation of different matrices and power parameters of two-element antenna for ultra-wideband (UWB) signal radiation is presented

articleTitle: Active Tongue Pulsed Transmitting Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A novel, UWB, pulsed, active, and transmitting antenna is proposed, which is based on the authors' developed and patented UWB antenna design concept called the tongue antenna. This antenna can be directly driven by a pulser circuit with a ferrite ring transformer which contributes to about 30% extra pulse peak amplitude. The active antenna design enables using of different types of pulse shaping diodes driven by 2...1000 V sources. Pulser active elements can be build with low-cost COTS rectifier diodes and its driver with MOSFET switchers that relax to a low-cost pulser design. Other design aspects of the active integrated antenna and pulser are reported including the measured data obtained with its prototype. In particular, derived experimental results include (i) 750 V @ 50 Omega with 2.5-3 ns rise time (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">imp</sub>=11 kW); (ii) 500 V @ 10 Omega with 1.7 ns rise time (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">imp</sub>=25 kW); (iii) 400 V @ 500 with 1.2ns rise time (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">imp</sub>=3.2 kW); (ii) 100V @ 50 Omega with 0.5 ns rise time (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">imp</sub>=0.2 kW)

articleTitle: The Development of the Pulse Electromagnetic Processes Measurement Unity Supporting System in Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: In the report the way of realization of the measurement chain according to the all-Union State Standard 8.540-2004 in Ukraine is stated. The basic element of such measurement chain is the Original Ukrainian Etalon (Standard) of the Pulse Electrical and Magnetic Fields Units. The report contains the information on the technical solutions of the Etalon elements, the procedure of its certification and main technical performance. The Etalon is a high-voltage pulse device with extreme temporal parameters. The amplitude of the electrical field pulses range has a band of 1 V/m to 200 kV/m, and the amplitude of the magnetic field pulses range covers the band of 10 mA/m to 50 A/m. The pulse rise time is less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>s. In the report ways of the Etalon application area widening for the certification and calibration of the high pulse voltages and currents are put for discussion.

articleTitle: Experimental Research of Loaded Conical Spirals Input Impedance Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The problem of the reflected current wave in spiral antennas was investigated. The method of suppressing the reflected current wave in conical spiral antennas was offered. Some results of experimental research of active resistor influence on input impedance characteristics for different cones and shield disposition are given

articleTitle: Symmetric Sampling Gate with Stored Charge Dumping
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The method of reducing the ultra wideband signal conversion error by a symmetric sampling gate has been considered in the given work. Characteristics of the sampling gate with stored charge dumping have been analyzed. It has been shown that the design of this sampling gate can deal without servo feedbacks in a sampler, as well as it permits to increase its sensitivity

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Signal Scattering from a Wirelines Buried in a Ground
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Model of ultra wideband signal scattering from the subsurface wirelines which diameter is small in comparison with length of a sounding wave and depth of its location in ground is considered. The created algorithm allows calculating the signals reflected by a cable which axis is parallel to air-ground interface, at any polarization and direction of an illumination. Results of calculations of ultra wideband signals reflected by cables, located in a lossy, dispersive ground, for various conditions of illumination are demonstrated and discussed

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation of the Ultrawideband FMCW Signal Propagation Through Ionospheric Radiochannel
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A theoretical description is given to the chirpsounder operation configuration in the mode of sounding the ionospheric radiochannel by the ultrawideband frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) signal. A preprocessing of the received signal is carried out using the frequency-compression method. It is shown that the result derived from processing an individual time sample is mathematically equivalent to a sounding of the radio channel by a complex-valued narrow-band impulse signal. Analysis of both in-phase and quadrature components of received FMCW signal at the output of intermediate frequency (IF) band-pass filter of the chirpsounder demonstrates a new possibility of recovering the transfer function of the HF radiochannel within the band of operating frequencies and the interval of time delays that are defined by the IF filter characteristics

articleTitle: Widening UWB System Coverage Zone by Repeaters-Regenerators
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) of the USA has limited communication coverage zone for pulse UWB systems by implementing power density mask on all transmitting devices. As result the UWB coverage area is not exceed a hundred meters. But it is possible to increase this area, still fulfilling the FCC limits, by adding one or more UWB repeaters around or along the path toward a destination receiver(s). The paper deals with the idea of such repeaters-regenerators and their implementations

articleTitle: The 100 GHz -1000 GHz Waves Scattering by Microcaverns in CVD-Diamond Windows
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The calculation results of wave scattering by internal non-homogeneities in real output CVD-diamond windows of megawatt gyrotrons in the 100 GHz-1000 GHz frequency range is presented. We have verified experimental result that up to 170-200 GHz the scattering is negligible, but above 200 GHz makes an appreciable contribution to absorption. The calculations have shown that near 1 THz the scattering becomes fundamental. For examined scatters geometry ~30-40% of total scattered energy scatters forward (to transmission line) and back (to gyrotron), ~70-60% encloses and absorbs in the disk volume. These results allowed formulating the demands to disk quality according to supposed set-up parameters

articleTitle: Focusing of Pulses by Plane Boundary of Nonstationary Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The free space Green's function for the time domain Maxwell equations in the 6D formulation is obtained. The integral equation for a boundary value problem is derived and the resolvent operator for a plasma half-space is constructed. Radiation transformation by newly created plasma is investigated. It is shown that transformed radiation of a point source is focused by a plasma plane boundary and this "time effect" looks like to that ''spatial effects" in the negative refractive index material

articleTitle: Mathematical Structure and Analysis of the Inductive and Electrostatic Fields of an Impulse Radiating Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Impulse radiating antennas are noted for their large on-axis radiation field. Little attention has been paid to their non-radiation inductive and electrostatic components which become dominant at small ranges. These fields may become important sources of electromagnetic interference electronic equipment located at small ranges. This paper provides a detailed derivation of the inductive and electrostatic fields in the frequency domain for a simplified model of an impulse radiating antenna (IRA), expressed in a spherical coordinate system. This derivation emphasizes meticulous execution in order to avoid apparent but, in practice, non-existing singularities. Such situations arise from the use of derived variables that appear in the denominator of transcendental functions

articleTitle: Features of Receiving Antennas Calculation in Fresnel Region
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: On the basis of geometrical optic's theory of diffraction are determined focusing properties of the receiving antennas located on any given distance from the transmitting antenna

articleTitle: Large Current Radiators
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The work is devoted to investigations aiming at developing special type of radiating antennas which are known as Harmuth's large current radiator. Physical and technical problems encountered when radiators designed and ways for their overcoming are discussed

articleTitle: Peculiarities of Videopulse Scanning Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Consideration is given to details of construction onboard active videopulse scanning antenna array (VPSAA) for radio-location applications. The influence of the relative sizes and the directional characteristics of individual radiators, their relative positioning on ability to maintenance of electronic scanning VPSAA in the necessary sector of space are investigated. Comparison of the directional characteristics and scanning ability of continuous aperture and antenna array is resulted.

articleTitle: Generator of Short High-Voltage Pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Generator of short pulses with characteristic pulse length approximately 1.5 ns and voltage amplitude 500 kV on the generator output has been successfully created and tested. The generator is built on the base of capacitive energy storages with using transformer in Tesla circuit and spark dischargers as high-voltage energy switches. T(TEM)-horn radiator is placed on the generator output. Switching time of output spark discharger of the generator was experimentally obtained to be less than 0.3 ns under breakdown voltage 500 kV. When using T-horn radiator having small directivity, pulse electric field intensity E approximately 100 V/m was obtained at a distance of r approximately 100 m from radiator opening. In this case E(r) was approximately 10 kV. Generators of such a type can be used for energy transmission at a distance with help of radiated electromagnetic pulses, and also for disinfecting treatment of various products in dielectric package by high (strong) pulse electric fields of T-wave.

articleTitle: Multielement Systems of Slots in Waveguides with Partial Dielectric Filling
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The investigation of possibility of the waveguide-slot antennas characteristics improvement with partial filling by dielectric was carried out. it is shown that the partial filling by dielectric of the waveguide makes it possible to increase gain and to expand operating band

articleTitle: Wide-Band Filters on Ferrite Resonators
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A rigorous electrodynamic theory of the bandwidth microwave filter design on the basis of ferrite resonators in a beyond-cut-off section of a rectangular waveguide is made up. The joint of two waveguides and the ferrite resonator are considered as the basic elements, for which the scattering matrixes are found. Two cases important for practice are considered: the filters consisting of a finite number of ferrite resonators, either identical or different in geometry and material parameters. For a system of identical elements the scattering matrix factors are determined through the polynomials of Chebyshev. The solution to the boundary problems for the system with different basic elements is found by the operator method. Numerical algorithms and methods of optimisation of the diffraction characteristics calculation for both single and coupled ferrite waveguide-resonator systems are developed

articleTitle: Development of a Method of Construction Radar-Tracking Images of the Air Targets
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: In article the approach to the decision of a task of formation of authentic bidimensional radar-tracking images in conditions of movement of the flying device on any trajectory with the account of trajectory instability his flight is opened. At formation of images the principle of inverse synthesizing of the aperture is used. The estimation of efficiency neural recognition of models of the air targets under bidimensional radar-tracking images is carried out

articleTitle: Application of Wavelets and Atomic Functions for Analysis of the Ultrawideband Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The wavelet analysis for the describing of the ultrawideband signals was applied. New type of the wavelet basis based on the atomic functions and Kravchenko windows was proposed. These wavelets as Kravchenko-Rvachev analytical wavelets as opposed to the being set of Kravchenko-Rvachev wavelets were called. The numerical characteristics of the Kravchenko-Rvachev analytical wavelets were calculated and with ones for other wavelets were compared. Earlier proposed quality functional, which was shown to be useful for the selection of the ultrawideband signal optimal wavelet basis, for the sooner created ultrawideband signal models and the Kravchenko-Rvachev analytical wavelets was calculated. The given results with ones for the other wavelet bases were compared. The Kravchenko-Rvachev analytical wavelets were shown to be effective for the ultrawideband signal describing

articleTitle: Shielding, Radioabsorbing and Scattering Materials for Decreasing of Disturbances and for Enhance of Efficiency of Radar Work
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Georadar of OKO-M1 type working at 400 MHz central frequency in combinations with different type of radioshielding and scattering materials have been studied to determine a possibility of an improvement of noise immunity and functional characteristics of georadar at various conditions. A number of experimental georadar covers of several types based on radioshielding, radioabsorbing and scattering materials has been produced and tested. The investigations have confirmed the fact that usage of a shielding cover is useful both for suppression of interference with up-land objects and for decrease of aerial disturbances. We found that such georadar cover can decrease a level of the aerial interference disturbance up to 30 dB, and undesirable signal reflected from a metal object placed near over georadar can been decreased on a value of 15...23 dB. A scan picture becomes more clean and readable when georadar shielding cover is used

articleTitle: The Effects of Short Exposition to Low-Energy Impulse Irradiation on Human Cells
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The effects of impulse radiation on human cells are presented. The chromatin state in interphase nucleus of human buccal epithelium cell was investigated as a parameter indicating the state of cell. For these investigations the original method of image processing was elaborated. It was shown that heterochromatin granule quantity increases under the influence of radiation

articleTitle: Study on Asymmetric Tapered Slotline Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Two novel but simple structures of asymmetric tapered slotline antenna (TSA) with synthesized radiation pattern is proposed. By adjusting the profiles of asymmetric conducting plates respectively, cutting the corrugated slots on side-edges, and setting a backed plate for single-TSA structure, the synthesized pattern in vertical plane can meet the requirement of specific application. The prototypes are considered as the scaled sample at 10 GHz for base-station of mobile communication system. A single-TSA sample is designed, its measured vertical pattern has 4deg beam tilting, null filling in the lower part, and suppressed side lobe (-19.9 dB) in the upper part; its HPBW in horizontal pattern is 65deg; it has 11.7 dBi of directive gain, and 3:1 frequency coverage (5.56~16.8 GHz) for VSWRles2:1. Another twin-TSA sample consists of a pair of asymmetric TSAs backed each other with a common excitation by a microstrip line, its simulated vertical pattern at 10 GHz has 7deg beam tilting in both sides, null filling in the lower part and suppressed side-lobe in the upper part; 34deg HPBW in vertical pattern and 60deg in horizontal pattern; and 8.4 dBi of directivity for each sides

articleTitle: Spherical Reflector Antenna Gain Optimization
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This report relates to the field of antenna systems for communicating between an earth station and a satellite. More particularly, it relates to a spherical reflector antenna system for broadband satellite communications systems operating in the microwave and millimeter wave frequency bands with low- and mid-earth orbiting satellites, which traverse the sky somewhat rapidly

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Signals and Choi-Williams Transform
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The Choi-Williams transform well known as the square time-frequency transform from Cohen class for the ultrawideband signal analysis was proposed. The general properties, advantages and disadvantages of the Choi-Williams transform were discussed. The ultrawideband signal models based on the atomic functions were analyzed numerically with the Choi-Williams transform and were discussed. The results of the ultrawideband signal analysis performed with the Choi-Williams transform usage with ones based on the Wigner transform and the short-time Fourier transform were compared

articleTitle: The New Scheme of the "Slicer" for Radiators of Powerful Nano-and Picosecond Pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The new scheme of formation of the short pulses is suggested. This scheme allows us to receive a bipolar step pulse on an output and it is possible to radiate received pulse into free space without sizeable power losses

articleTitle: Simulation of Impulse Exciting a Slotted Cone Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: An initial boundary electromagnetic problem for a bicone structure with longitudinal slots is investigated. The problem solution method is based on using the Meller Fock integral transforms and the semi-inversion method. Analytical solutions of the problem are obtained for special cases of this structure. Slots effects are studied

articleTitle: Source of Ultra-Wide Band Radiation in Millimeter Waver Range
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Ultra-wide band (UWB) sources in millimeter wavelength region are of great interest for many applications, including, for example, super-high-speed data communications. We present a UWB source in millimeter wavelength region based on electronic beam modulation by comparatively low-frequency (relative to carrier frequency) regular and noise signals. The presented set-up can be employed as a generator of coherent radiation, generator of UWB signal and noise generator

articleTitle: Exact Reversal of a Multi-Mode Waveguide Bolometer Problem for Transmitting Mode Simulations of Broadband Detector Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: An exact reciprocal formulation is proposed for the rigorous modeling of bolometric systems in transmitting mode, including the case of a bolometric detector in a multi-mode waveguide. The formulation provides an exact reversal of the bolometer operation from the actual receiving mode to the effective transmitting one so that all the parametric dependencies of power absorbed in receiving mode are reproduced identically by the power radiated in transmitting mode. The formulation of this kind allows one to compute, among other properties, accurate angular sensitivity patterns of complicated multi-mode quasi-optical detector systems by considering much simpler simulation problem of modeling the systems in equivalent transmitting mode

articleTitle: Diffraction Waves on a Spherical Resonator Segment
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The application and the generalization of the regularization tasks of the diffraction of electromagnetic waves on a sphere with the circular aperture are proposed. We examine the diffraction of the plane wave, on sphere. We solve auxiliary integral equations of Abel's type and select main parts of functional equations by introducing the small parameters. As a result we obtain disconnected linear algebraic equations of second kind of Fredholm's type. New possibilities of improvement of computational algorithms and different characteristics of spherical antennas (radiation pattern, radiation power, field profiles of different resonant modes, radar cross section, wideband signals) are discussed

articleTitle: The Mechanism of Collinear Longitudinal Slot and Microstrip Eigenwaves Interaction
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The mechanism of collinear longitudinal slot and microstrip eigenwaves interaction is investigated. The possibility of main eigenwave of microstrip (the T-mode) transformation into surface mode theoretically is shown. The frequency bands of effective transformation experimentally are established. The counter lines of field structures are presented. The pattern characteristics are investigated

articleTitle: The GPR Response of a Subsurface Objects and its Use for Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The present work reports the results of laboratory measurements of the real part of dielectric permittivity ε' and dielectric loss tangent tg (δ) of sandy and clayey soils as a function of soil moisture (X) uniformly distributed throughout the volume and of electromagnetic field frequency. Also, the theoretical research of the dependence the reflected signal shape on the humidity profile was realized.

articleTitle: Isolated 2D Plasma Resonator Illuminated by Transient Source
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Excitation of isolated 2D plasma circular resonator by transient external source is investigated. Study is carried out on base of Green's function approach. Analytical solution is obtained in frequency domain. Attention is focused upon the spectrum of excited fields

articleTitle: On Transient Radiation of a Linear Impedance Antenna Exited by the Electron Bunch
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A linear impedance antenna of transient radiation exited by the electron bunch scattered on its end face is considered. The radiation is analyzed at the stage of a bunch approach to the antenna. The radiation is an induced or diffraction one and has a nature of forced oscillations. The radiation spectrum has an extremum. The dispersion equation of an antenna is derived. The expressions for the components of the discrete spectrum of the current force and the strengths of electric and magnetic fields, radiated by the antenna, are constructed as a series in the antenna eigen functions. It is shown, that the antenna element is radiative if the strengths of extrinsic and intrinsic electric fields are in phase and in antiphase accordingly to the antenna current. In this case the extrinsic electric field strength accelerates the conductivity electrons and the intrinsic electric field strength brakes electrons, producing the radiation of latter ones

articleTitle: Impulse Formation by Spatial-Time Phase Encoding
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper comprises of the analysis of basic properties of the spatial-time signal upon emission of the phase-shift keyed signal by each element of the active phased antenna array. Mathematical modeling results are presented in terms of the phase-shift/code-shift keyed (FKM) signals with random even phase distribution

articleTitle: The Apply of the Expert Systems of Signal Processing with Frequency and Polarizations Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the principles of the system construction of the signal processing with frequency and polarizations descriptions for the complex missions of air traffic control and air supervision. The expedience of consulting model of data processing is considered.

articleTitle: The Application of Integral Equations for 2-D Diffraction Problems of Electromagnetic Pulses on Metal and Dielectric Bodies
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The space-time integral equations are solved based on separation of the static part and follow-up application of collocation method for 2-D problems. Basis functions are built on the whole surface of the complex area and satisfy the conditions on metal ridges. The time dependence is approximated by splines and Lagrange polynomials

articleTitle: Radiation of Ultra-Wideband Signals by Pulse Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A complex approach to computer-aided design of the broadband pulse antenna for UWB WPAN communication system is presented in the paper. Investigation of the time- and frequency-domain characteristics of the antenna, ultra-wideband signals and properties of the radiated field are described. The paper discusses parameters and the limitation of UWB signals' spectrums. Time-domain characteristics and spectrums of different UWB signals are investigated. Results of calculation of the electric field radiated by the antenna are presented

articleTitle: Influence of Mutual Coupling on Spatial-Time Characteristics of Antenna Array Excited by Short Pulse Signal
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A method is proposed for calculation of radiated field from an antenna array excited by a pulse signal taking into account coupling between elements of the array. The method is valid for a conventional antenna array as well as for a retrodirective antenna array. The influence of antenna array parameters was also investigated

articleTitle: Estimation of the Target Detection Radar Noise Stability at the Ultrawideband Jamming Influence
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The field structure formation of an ultra wideband signal on the input of the target detection radar receiver device with working frequency 1 GHz is considered. The algorithms of the fields temporary structure definition based on the equations Kirghoff-Kothler with the subsequent estimation of the ultra-short impulse accidental jamming power characteristics necessary for specification of accepted signals processing algorithms are offered

articleTitle: Effects of Resonant Scattering of Intensive Fields by Layer with Weakly Kerr-Like Dielectric Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The layer with weakly Kerr-like dielectric nonlinearity is considered. The results of a numerical analysis of the diffraction problem of a plane wave on the weakly nonlinear object with positive and negative value of the susceptibility are shown. The effects: non-uniform shift of resonant frequency of the diffraction characteristics of a weakly nonlinear dielectric layer; itself the channeling of a field; increase of the angle of the transparency of the nonlinear layer when growth of intensity of the field (at positive value of the susceptibility); de-channeling of a field (at negative value of the susceptibility) are found out

articleTitle: Time and Amplitude Centre of an Impulse Wavebeam
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Some characteristics are investigated for an impulse wave beam, which is produced by currents on a plane. In particular, the term "time center" is introduced that describes curvature center of the radiated impulse wave front; its behavior while propagating is analyzed

articleTitle: New Edition of the Ukrainian Technical Electromagnetic Compatability Adequacy Confirmation Order
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This report renders the ground of the necessity of the preparation of the new edition of the Technical Electromagnetic Compatibility Adequacy Confirmation Order (TEMCO), ratified in December, 31, 2003. The preparation of the new TEMCO edition is included in the standardization sheet of the Ministry of Industrial Policy of Ukraine. Preliminary results of the new TEMCO edition preparation produced by the task group, the authors of the report are affiliated with, will be put for discussion.

articleTitle: The Research of General Aviation ADS-B Base on TD-SCDMA Wide Band Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: With the development of general aviation, China needs a kind of airborned communication terminal, which is affordable, reliable and convenient. This terminal can broadcast its ranging data periodically which will be received by the aircrafts in the same airspace, so it can realize ADS function. In this paper, based on TD-SCDMA international standard, it introduces two communication modes named "controlled" and "self-organized" used by the airborned terminals. Airborned terminals will realize the wideband data link through the handover flexible between two communication modes and update reserved slots table dynamic. It will assure the safety and regular of ATC through the method in this paper

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: Effects on Placing Wideband Omnidirectional Spiral Antenna on Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A problem of radiation of square spiral antenna placed on an aircraft fuselage is considered. The aircraft is approximated as an elliptic cylinder with trapezoidal wings. The problem is solved by hybrid technique which uses FEM (finite element method) for near-field calculation and UTD (uniform theory of diffraction) for directional pattern and surface currents computation. The imperfect conductance of the fuselage and wings is approximated via impedance boundary conditions

articleTitle: Description Possibility of the Pulse Antennas's Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The possibility of description of the pulse antennas characteristics based on the ultra short pulse signals energy measuring in time domain is studied in the article. Pulse antenna input reflection ratio and its performance index definition is given in the article. These parameters experimental measurement methodology is also described in the article

articleTitle: Possibilities of Extending the Stop and Pass Bandwidths of the Microwave Antenna-Filters by Means of a Dielectric Resonant Scatterer
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of the microwave electronic systems (ES) are highly actual and very important. Usually the noise delay is realized via various stop-band filters on the basis of arrays, volume metal resonators, etc. But those possess some drawbacks such as a big mass and relatively considerable dimensions and volume. Effective suppression of the undesirable signals may be achieved using a sole dielectric resonant scatterers (DRS) combined with a rectangular waveguide radiators. Sometimes it is necessary to extend the stop and pass bandwidths of such antenna-filters

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Control of Spherical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental research of irradiation shift influence on radiation pattern are prepared. Scanning limits of antenna beam are determined. Some recommendations for scanning spherical antennas projecting are given

articleTitle: Application of Filtration and Pixel-by-Pixel Transform Procedures for Ultrawideband Radiometry Images Visual Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Influence estimation of filtration and pixel-by-pixel transform procedures of the experimentally received with the help of ultrawideband radiometer images on quality of objects authentication by an operator is considered. The new algorithm of image histogram transforms, allowing receiving the required brightness probability density, is offered

articleTitle: Complex Modes of a Dielectric Covered Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Sources and related components to support high power electromagnetic (HPEM) ultra-wideband systems are of growing importance. The ultra-wideband domain is characterized by a bandwidth ratio, br=(f <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">high</sub>/f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>)>10 with a nominal center frequency in the GHz range. Shielded microstrips and coplanar waveguides may find increasing application for developing advanced ultra-wideband systems. Dielectric covered ground planes are often part of microstrip or coplanar waveguides and properties of their propagation modes need to be better understood. Over the years, several different techniques and theories have been used to analyze the propagation modes of dielectrics covered planes. In this paper, expressions for the transverse wave numbers within the dielectric and above it are derived for two types of modes, denoted as transverse magnetic and transverse electric (TM and TE). In contrast to earlier work our fields are transverse to the direction normal to the dielectric interface, not to the direction of propagation. In addition to modes with real transverse wave numbers, modes with complex transverse wave numbers are shown to occur in conjugate pairs whose members can be combined into patterns with sinusoidal variation in the direction normal to the surface of the dielectric. Some of the results are presented in tables in which the propagation constants, computed from the wave equation, are also given

articleTitle: Synthesis of Resonant Waveguide Antenna with Various Requirements in the Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The front-to-rear factor of resonant waveguide antenna is optimized in a wide frequency band by means of statement and solving the appropriate synthesis problem. The variational statement of the problem allows to take into account the requirements to the front-to-rear factor in the operating frequency band as well as outside of this band. The direct optimization of the used functionals is carried out by the modified coordinate descent method. The results of numerical modeling are shown

articleTitle: Comparison Characteristics of Small-Size UWB Receiving Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The evaluation of obtainable sensitivity of small-size magnetic and electric antennas made on the basis of numerical solution of UWB electromagnetic pulse registration in case when the resistance element is used as an antenna load is presented in the given work. The connection between antenna characteristics (geometric and electric) and the amplitude of a useful signal induced in the antenna has been established. The dependences of received electromagnetic pulse waveforms and antenna sensitivity on the resistive load value of electric and magnetic dipoles in case that the electric dipole length is equal to the loop diameter of the magnetic dipole are also given in the report

articleTitle: Coupling Effects in Resistive UWB Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The self- and mutual impedances of elements in the dissipative antenna array are known to involve radiative resistances and loss resistances. This paper is dedicated to analyzing the structure of the mutual impedance between resistive load elements and its effect on the radiation efficiency of the array

articleTitle: Shaping Device of Nanosecond Coherent Radio Pulses of SHF Oscillations with Heightened Power
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Traveling wave resonator, the waves of which spread along the waveguide ring in opposite directions, is offered and analyzed. The processes of energy accumulating in the ring resonator and its high-speed outlet from the resonator are considered. The advantages of offered device in comparison with known devices of the similar purpose are shown

articleTitle: Qualitative Analysis of Elementary Antennas Impulse Radiation
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the non-stationary structure of simple antenna fields (the electric dipole, the vibrator, the system of dipoles) with the help of the qualitative theory methods for the ordinary differential equations (ODE). The qualitative analysis is of interest because numerical research meets the certain difficulties in vicinities of the vector field critical points, and qualitative methods are effective in these cases in particular. Therefore the combination of qualitative and numerical methods is the most expedient and economical approach in the analysis of electromagnetic fields. The strategy of qualitative theory application to the analysis of pulse fields of simple antennas in free space, and also the results in this area received to the present time are discussed

articleTitle: Power Combining in UWB Sources
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The accumulation of the UWB signal power by combining the power in many relatively weak unit sources has been considered in the given report. The basic active component in generators of UWB ultrashortpulse (USP) signals is the device switching between modes of high and low conductivity. The most effective way of developing the power USP technique is to create a small spectrum of generic generating modules. The generating power can be increased only by increasing the device volume, i.e. by increasing sizes (from one to three dimensions).

articleTitle: Field Radiation of the Ring of the Radial Current from Screened Sphere with the Aperture
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The algorithm of calculation of fields of the radial electric current ring, placed within sphere with a circular aperture is obtained. The electromagnetic fields created by a source at presence of considered structure have been simulated, and also polar patterns have been constructed

articleTitle: Energy Characteristics of Multielement Resonator-Slot Radiators
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The problem of magnetic currents distributions definition is solved using the induced magnetomotive method for the structure: "coupling slots in a wall of an infinite rectangular waveguide-rectangular volume resonator-radiating slot in an infinite metal screen". The numerical calculations are carried out and the graphs of energetic characteristics for such systems are presented

articleTitle: Analysis of Influence of Aperture Finiteness on Wideband Signals of Microwave Introscopy using Plane Wave Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Using plane wave decomposition the influence of finiteness of the antenna aperture on wideband signals of microwave introscopy has been considered. Distortions of the frequency characteristic and change of the form of the synthesized spatial signal of reflection have been considered under reduction of the size of the antenna aperture and under reduction of distance up to target. The opportunity of occurrence of additional false peaks in the spatial signal has been demonstrated

articleTitle: Cell Effects of Electromagnetic Radiation
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The effects of electromagnetic radiation on cells and cell organelles are reviewed. The original results of studies of the influence of monochrome and impulse radiation on human cells are presented. The heterochromatin granule quantity was investigated as a parameter indicating the state of human cell. It was shown that heterochromatin granule quantity and cell membrane permeability increases under the influence of radiation, which is the significant component of general cell stress reaction

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Signals Transformation by Linear Antennas in Reception Mode
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: The necessity of separate solution to a problem of ultra wideband signals reception by antennas has been analyzed. One of problem-solving approaches was viewed as time domain analysis. It is shown that the wave drag discrete change on antenna terminals caused by difference in wave impedance between antenna and transmission line, have an effect on signal waveform at receiving aerial output. It has been suggested a solution to the problem of unrestricted time dependency waves reception by linear antennas. On the basis of suggested solution, a time and frequency dependencies of voltage on dipole terminals has been formed

articleTitle: The Quantitative Analysis of Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: A method for presenting the result of ground penetrating radar (GPR) data processing in the form of structural model of the medium being probed that is obtained on the basis of the quantitative analysis of radar traces showing the reflecting boundaries and electrophysical parameters is considered in this paper. The basis for the method developed are results of studying the features of the reflected signal formations in inhomogeneous media. The method enables to algorithmize the construction process for the structural model of the model of the medium being probed, to decrease labour consumption for radar trace processing and to reduce human factor effect.

articleTitle: Drawing Defendable Conclusions from Effects Tests using Pulse Illumination of Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Engineers spend a great deal of time and effort collecting effects data on the illumination of electronic systems by electromagnetic waves. The effects can include upset or damage to the devices. The overall goal of these data is to draw conclusions about conditions that will allow the prediction of future failures of electronic systems of the same type or application. Illumination sources can include lightning, electromagnetic interference or high-power microwaves. It is rare that the engineer is allowed to take sufficient data to meet the usual statistical tests for conclusions about the data, yet those tests limit the applicability of the conclusions. This paper will outline the general statistical requirements by presenting general models. Applicability of those models will be extended using physical constraints and examples will be shown

articleTitle: Algorithms of Forming and Correlation Properties of Some Classes of Polyphase Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper is concerned with the particularities of the new class of complex (polyphase) signals created based on the maximum length sequences (M-sequences) and investigation of their properties based on the spectral and correlation analyses

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of the Microwave Transducer of the Complex Reflection Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: This paper presents the mathematical model of three-port microwave parametric transducer of the complex reflection coefficient. The system of nonlinear equations relating the samples of output signal to magnitude and argument of the reflection coefficient as well as the transducer parameters is obtained. The ways solving this system by means of iterative techniques are considered. Linearization of the system measurement equations is performed to enhance processing speed.

articleTitle: Changing of Pulse Complexity in Modulated Dielectric Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Using an exactly solvable model of a process the modulation of an electromagnetic field in a time-varying medium is investigated. A correlation between the Hurst's index for process and its complexity in this case is shown

articleTitle: Some Aspects of UWB Signal Interference
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd International Conference on Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals
abstract: Some problems of UWB signal interference are considered without making conventional simplifying assumptions. The possibility of applying impulse response and other dynamic characteristics to vector electromagnetic problems is discussed. We formulate a general superposition principle applicable to electromagnetic fields and give a generalized description of the interference field and its polarization state, suitable for the analysis of any signals, including UWB signals

articleTitle: The using of Ultrawideband Canal in Problem of Time Scale Comparison
